Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom

summary: Initial security posture discovery for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is concerned about SOC2/ISO, SSO, and encryption. Redwood AE/SE walked through controls, deployment options, and proposed next steps for providing attestation docs and integration guides. Customer requested pilot pricing and a follow-up planning call for on-prem/private deployment evaluation.
topics: SSO / SAML integration and IdP support (Okta)
RBAC and permission model for tenant/isolation
Audit logs, retention, and exports for compliance
Encryption at rest / KMS integration / HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, isolation)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood. We'll do a quick security posture run through - high level then Priya will do the technical.
[00:15] Ethan: Hi, Ethan here. We're evaluating options - hosted vs dedicated vs private - and security is the gating factor, mostly SOC2, SSO, and encryption.
[00:30] Priya: Awesome. Quick agenda: compliance attestation, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs/retention, KMS/encryption, devops access. We'll try to keep to 45-60 minutes.
[00:45] Maya: Sounds good. We have a regulatory requirement to keep logs for 7 years, so retention is a big one.
[00:58] Liam: Also need to confirm if Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for private deployments - can't have provider-owned keys for some datasets.
[01:15] Jordan: Totally understood. To start, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certifications for our hosted control plane; we can share the attestation report under NDA. For Private - VPC and on-prem - customers can use their own KMS, and we support HSM integrations for Dedicated/Private. We'll drop the certs after the call.
[01:40] Ethan: When you say "drop the certs" you mean a PDF or an access portal? We have procurement that needs the actual report.
[01:50] Jordan: PDF attestation and a summary page; if you need the full report we can provide it under an NDA. I'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts. Link example: https://redwood.example/security/soc2.pdf (placeholder).
[02:10] Maya: Ok. Also, does Redwood support SAML SSO? We run Okta and we need SSO + SCIM for user provisioning.
[02:22] Priya: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM. We have an Okta guide; I'll share integration steps and an example metadata file. Note: for Private installs, SCIM provisioning depends on network routing but it's supported.
[02:40] Liam: Do you have RBAC broken down by org/team/route? We need least-privilege controls, audit trail per token.
[02:50] Priya: We have role-based permissions: org-admin, project-admin, dev, viewer, plus route-level policies. You can scope API keys to model routes and set per-key quotas. Audit logs capture token IDs and request metadata.
[03:10] Maya: Is audit log retention configurable per customer? We might need to export logs to our SIEM for long-term retention.
[03:20] Jordan: Yes - Hosted provides logs via our console with 90 days by default, longer retention is an add-on; Dedicated and Private let you configure export to S3/Cloud Storage and push to your SIEM. We'll document the export formats (JSON/NDJSON).
[03:45] Ethan: For compliance, we need immutable audit trails and the ability to sign logs. Is that supported?
[03:55] Priya: We don't currently offer cryptographic log signing as a managed feature, but with Dedicated/Private you can deploy your own signing pipeline when exporting logs. We do provide tamper-evident write-once storage options if you need object-lock S3 on the export side.
[04:20] Liam: About encryption - TLS in transit is a given, but for at-rest encryption, can we bring our own KMS?
[04:30] Priya: Yes. For Hosted, we use provider-managed keys by default but support customer-managed keys (CMK) for enterprise customers with a contract. For Dedicated and Private, you can bring your own KMS or HSM. The key wrapping and envelope encryption patterns are standard. We'll share a KMS integration doc.
[04:55] Maya: Any certifications for KMS/HSM integrations? We need to map to our control framework.
[05:05] Jordan: We can provide technical mapping docs and control narratives that map Redwood controls to common frameworks - SOC 2, ISO, and we'll include KMS/HSM controls.
[05:20] Ethan: Network isolation - for Private we need an air-gapped option for some workloads. Is that something you support?
[05:30] Priya: We offer an on-prem package that can be deployed air-gapped; it requires a different support path and we usually do a professional services engagement for initial setup. For VPC Private we do customer-managed networking, peering, and strict egress rules.
[05:50] Liam: How about data flow for prompt inputs and outputs - we need assurance data isn't retained in the hosted model longer than configured.
[06:00] Jordan: By default hosted keeps prompt logs for 30 days for debugging and analytics, but Enterprise customers can opt into reduced retention or no retention. We support per-customer retention policies, and you can opt out of logging entirely for sensitive routes.
[06:25] Maya: That's good but we need a contract clause - specifically no retention for PII-backed requests unless encrypted and with consent.
[06:35] Jordan: We can include that in an enterprise contract and document the data handling rules.
[06:45] Ethan: Who has access internally to the hosted tenant? Are there service accounts, ops, SRE, that can read raw prompts?
[06:55] Priya: Access is strictly role-gated and logged. Only platform engineers with approved change requests and with justification can access production logs, and access is time-limited. We do triple-A: SSO, RBAC, and MFA for our staff.
[07:15] Liam: Do you have a separation between control plane and data plane? We need control plane access without exposure to customer data.
[07:25] Priya: Yes - control plane is distinct. Customer data flows through the data plane which can be isolated in a Dedicated or Private deployment. Control plane metadata (billing, routing) does not include raw prompts.
[07:40] Maya: On the Dedicated offering, do customers get a dedicated GPU pool and VPC peering?
[07:48] Jordan: Correct. Dedicated is reserved capacity in a customer-isolated environment, with VPC peering and dedicated GPU pools. That reduces the blast radius and improves predictability.
[08:05] Ethan: We have latency constraints for inference - 99th percentile under 250ms. Can you guarantee that on Dedicated?
[08:15] Priya: With Dedicated configured to your SLA and capacity commit, we can target latency SLOs. We'll need to model throughput and sequence lengths; we can run a benchmark pilot to validate.
[08:35] Liam: About logging export format: do you include KV cache or token-level data? We want metadata but not raw token content in long-term logs.
[08:45] Priya: Default audit logs include request metadata, client IP, model used, token counts, and an opaque request id. Raw prompts are stored separately and can be excluded from exports. For compliance we recommend exporting redacted logs to SIEM.
[09:05] Maya: Do you offer data residency guarantees (e.g., EU-only processing)?
[09:12] Jordan: Yes, we have region controls - Hosted customers can select region for processing; Dedicated and Private give full control over location. We support European regions and can ensure no cross-border processing if required.
[09:30] Ethan: Ok. A couple of procurement items - do you provide a SOC2 bridge letter and a data processing agreement (DPA)?
[09:40] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide a bridge letter along with the SOC2 report and a standard DPA; we can discuss any specific clauses you need.
[09:55] Liam: For SAML, how does session expiration work? We want short-lived sessions with token rotation.
[10:05] Priya: Session TTL is configurable and we can integrate with your IdP for SAML assertions, short token lifetimes, and automatic refresh. We also support OIDC for some customers.
[10:25] Maya: Are there native features for secret scanning or PII detection?
[10:32] Priya: We have optional pre-processing filters for PII detection and redaction that can run inline or asynchronously. For higher security you can combine that with private deployments to remove sensitive fields prior to storage.
[10:50] Ethan: For Dedicated pricing, what's the commitment cadence? monthly or annual?
[10:58] Jordan: Typically we do monthly billing but offer discounts for annual commits. We'll send a pilot pricing estimate.
[11:10] Liam: On audit logs, is there an immutable chain or sequence numbers to detect deletions?
[11:20] Priya: We include sequence numbers and tamper-evident export options on Dedicated/Private via storage features like S3 object-lock.
[11:35] Maya: Any pen-test results or vulnerability timelines you can share?
[11:42] Jordan: We run quarterly pentests and VDP program; we can share redacted reports and remediation timelines.
[11:55] Ethan: Who signs the BAA? We have PHI in some prompts and need a BAA.
[12:03] Jordan: We do sign BAAs for customers handling PHI; legal will handle that - I'll loop in our contracts lead when we proceed.
[12:15] Maya: Ok, that covers a lot. Could we go deeper on how RBAC maps to API keys and routes?
[12:25] Priya: Sure - we have API keys that are scoped to project and route. Example: key A -> model/chat-route-1, limited to generate episodes X per minute. Team-level roles govern who can create keys and who can view audit trails. We also support temporary keys via the API.
[12:50] Liam: Are there any gotchas with rate-limiting and burst capacity that could affect compliance? For example, logs dropped under heavy load?
[13:00] Priya: We do best-effort durable logging; we don't drop logs. Under extreme load we buffer and export; for compliance customers we recommend Dedicated with guaranteed throughput.
[13:20] Ethan: We want to run a POC focusing on a regulated workflow, probably on Dedicated or Private. Timeline is Q1 2027 for a pilot.
[13:32] Jordan: Great. For pilots we usually do a 4-6 week engagement: initial benchmarking, integration (SSO/KMS), and then a regression test. Priya will own the tech plan.
[13:45] Priya: I'll propose a pilot plan: week 1 onboarding and infra; week 2 SSO/KMS; week 3 workload testing and logs export; week 4 review and go/no-go.
[14:00] Maya: That sounds reasonable. For the on-prem option we need a professional services estimate.
[14:08] Jordan: We'll include that in the pricing packet.
[14:15] Liam: Can we get a sample RBAC JSON and a sample audit log export?
[14:22] Priya: Yes - I'll send sample RBAC policy JSON and a redacted NDJSON export example.
[14:30] Ethan: Any limitations for SCIM group sync frequency? We have a fast-changing org.
[14:38] Priya: SCIM sync can be scheduled; near-realtime sync is available depending on IdP settings. We'll document recommended cadence.
[14:50] Maya: Are there separate SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[14:58] Jordan: Yes - Hosted has standard availability SLAs; Dedicated comes with an SLA aligned to reserved capacity. We'll include SLA language in the contracts.
[15:15] Ethan: For the encryption KMS flow, is ephemeral keys used per-request or per-session?
[15:22] Priya: We use envelope encryption with ephemeral data keys per-session typically; master keys are in your KMS. That minimizes surface area.
[15:40] Liam: Any insights on how you handle model updates without impacting auditability?
[15:48] Priya: Model changes are versioned and we surface rollout notes; you can pin model versions for a route to ensure reproducible behaviour. All changes are in the control plane and logged.
[16:05] Maya: Final procurement question: what SCC or GDPR support do you provide for Data Subject Requests?
[16:15] Jordan: We provide DSR tooling to retrieve or delete customer data per contract, and data processing addendums cover the legal basis; we'll share the DSR flow doc.
[16:30] Ethan: Great. I think that's the bulk of our questions. Next steps?
[16:36] Jordan: Recap: we'll share SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS and SAML docs, sample RBAC and log exports, pricing for Dedicated/pilot, and schedule a pilot planning call. Priya will own the technical deliverables.
[16:55] Maya: We'll get back with date availability for the planning call and share the compliance owner to sign NDAs if needed.
[17:05] Liam: I'll send our log retention requirements and any special clauses we need in DPA.
[17:15] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else from Redwood?
[17:20] Priya: No, we'll follow up with the artifact bundle by Thursday.
[17:30] Ethan: Thanks, appreciate the thorough review.
[17:35] Jordan: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[17:40] (call ends)

Notes/artifacts referenced: SOC2/ISO attestation (to be shared), SAML/Okta guide (link), KMS integration whitepaper (to be shared), sample RBAC JSON and NDJSON log export (to be shared), pilot pricing spreadsheet (to be shared).
